notes:
AUDIT 2026-10-03 (NVIDIA dense/sparse convention re-verified from the primary Ada whitepaper PDF, no values changed): NVIDIA's Ada GPU architecture whitepaper prints its consumer spec tables in the same 'DENSE/SPARSE' form with the footnote 'Effective TOPS / TFLOPS using the Sparsity Feature'. AD102 appendix: 'Peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP16 Accumulate 330.3/660.6', 'Peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate 165.2/330.4', 'Peak BF16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate 165.2/330.4', 'Peak TF32 Tensor TFLOPS 82.6/165.2', 'Peak INT8 Tensor TOPS 660.6/1321.2', 'Peak INT4 Tensor TOPS 1321.2/2642.4'. So the five dense:false rows on this record - bf16 330.4, tf32 165.2, fp8 660.6, int8 1321.2, int4 2642.4 - are each the SPARSE column of the printed pair, with the dense twin stored separately. Correct. The fp8 660.6 row is the paper's 'FP16 with FP16 accumulate' rate; Ada has no native FP8 accumulate path, which is why this figure equals the FP16-accumulate FP16 number rather than half of it. 
INTERCONNECT FILLED 2026-10-04: interconnect was empty; it now reads ['pcie-gen4'], from the vendor's own spec table (source the GeForce RTX 4090 product page's 'Technology Support' row). SCALE-UP IS ABSENT AND THAT IS THE POINT: this part has no NVLink and no other GPU-to-GPU fabric, so the host link is the ONLY interconnect a multi-GPU deployment has. Do not infer a fabric from the presence of a PCIe value, and do not read the Gen number as a multi-GPU capability.
